title: Creating Limitations
use_cases: Use when balancing gameplay to prevent deus ex machina outcomes.
Implement when designing character spellcasting to enforce resource costs.
Configure when defining maximum range, duration, or power of spells.
Use when adding fatigue or cooldown mechanics to constrain usage.
Implement when setting prerequisites or failure conditions for magic.
Configure when creating realistic constraints on magical effects.
content:
Limitations are important in magic systems. Your magic system shouldn’t be so convenient that the magic bearer summons up a spell, curse, channels a thing-a-ma-bob right when they’re about to die. This falls into the deus ex machina area. Basically, it’s a little too convenient. Magic can do a lot of things, but it can’t do everything.

With that in mind, below are a few of the limitations you can use to make your magic system more believable.
